first: चौ॰—गै स्त्रम सकल सुखी नूप भयऊ। निज आस्त्रम तापस लेइ गयऊ॥
en: His tiredness gone, the king felt refreshed, and the ascetic took him to his hermitage. Seeing that the sun had set, he gave him a seat, and then spoke to him gently.

first: को तुम्ह कस बन फिरहु अकेले। सुन्दर जुबा जीव पर हेले॥
en: 'Who are you, and why do you wander alone in the forest, young and handsome, risking your life? You have the marks of an emperor; seeing them, I feel great concern for you.'

first: नाम प्रताप-भानु अवनीसा। तासु सचिव मैँ सुनहु मुनीसा॥
en: 'Great sage, listen: there is a king named Pratapabhanu, and I am his minister. While hunting I lost my way, and by great good luck I have come and seen your feet.'

first: हम कहँ दुर्लभ दरस तुम्हारा। जानत हौँ कछु भल हाेनिहारा॥
en: 'A sight of you is rare for people like us; I feel something good is about to happen.' The sage said, 'Son, it has grown dark, and your city is seventy yojanas away.'

first: दो॰—निसा-घोर गम्भीर-बन, पन्थ न सुनहु सुजान।
en: 'Listen, wise one: the night is very dark, the forest is deep, and there is no path. Knowing this, stay here tonight and go at daybreak.'

first: तुलसी जसि भवितव्यता, तैसी मिलइ सहाइ।
en: Tulsi says: as fate is, so is the help one finds. If fate does not come to a man, it takes him to where it waits.

first: चौ॰—भलेहि नाथ आयसु धरि सीसा। बाँधि तुरग तरु बैठ महीसा॥
en: 'Very well, Lord,' said the king, accepting his word. He tied his horse to a tree and sat down. He praised the ascetic in many ways, bowed at his feet and called himself lucky.

first: पुनि बोलेउ मृदु गिरा सुहाई। जानि पिता प्रभु करउँ ढिठाई॥
en: Then he spoke in a pleasant, gentle voice: 'Lord, I take the liberty of thinking of you as my father. Great sage, treat me as your son and servant, and tell me your name.'

first: तेहि न जान नृप नृपहि सो जाना। भूप सुहृद से कपट सयाना॥
en: The king did not know him, but he knew the king. The king was pure of heart, while he was skilled in deceit. He was an enemy, a warrior and a king as well, and he wished to gain his ends by trickery.

first: समुझि राज-पुख दुखित अराती। अवाँ अनल इव सुलगइ छाती॥
en: The enemy grieved, thinking of the king's royal happiness, and his heart smouldered like the fire in a potter's kiln. Hearing the king's simple words, and remembering his hatred, he rejoiced inwardly.

first: दो॰—कपट बोरि बानी मृदुल, बोलेउ जुगुति समेत।
en: He spoke soft words soaked in deceit and full of cunning: 'My name now is Beggar. I have no wealth and no home.'

first: चौ॰—कह नृप जे बिज्ञान निधाना। तुम्ह सारिखे गलित अभिमाना॥
en: The king said, 'Those who, like you, are treasures of wisdom and free of pride always keep themselves hidden. They think it wise in every way to dress poorly.'

first: तेहि तेँ कहहिँ सन्त स्त्रुति टेरे। परम अकिञ्चन प्रिय हरि केरे॥
en: 'That is why saints and the Vedas declare that those who own nothing are dear to Hari. Before a poor, homeless beggar like you, even Brahma and Shiva would feel unsure.'

first: जोसि साेसि तव चरन नमामी। मो पर कृपा करिय अब स्वामी॥
en: 'Whoever you may be, I bow at your feet. Lord, now be kind to me.' Seeing the king's natural love and his strong trust in him,

first: सब प्रकार राजहि अपनाई। बोलेउ अधिक सनेह जनाई॥
en: he won the king over completely and spoke, showing even more affection: 'Listen, king, I tell you truly: I have lived here for a very long time.'

first: दो॰—अब लगि माेहि न मिलेउ कोउ, मैँ न जनावउँ काहु।
en: 'Till now no one has met me, and I have made myself known to no one. Fame in the world is like fire; it burns the forest of penance.'

first: सो॰—तुलसी देखि सुबेखु, भूलहिँ मूढ़ न चतुर नर।
en: Tulsi says: seeing a fine appearance, not only fools but even clever men are deceived. Look at the lovely peacock: its voice is sweet as nectar, yet it eats snakes.

first: चौ॰—ता तेँ गुपुत रहउँ जग माहीँ। हरि तजि किमपि प्रयोजन नाहीँ॥
en: 'So I stay hidden in the world; apart from Hari I need nothing. The Lord knows everything without being told. Tell me, what is gained by pleasing people?'

first: तुम्ह सुचि सुमति परम प्रिय माेरे। प्रीति प्रतीति मोहि पर ताेरे॥
en: 'You are pure and wise and very dear to me; you have love and trust in me. Son, if I hide anything from you now, I would be guilty of a grave fault.'

first: जिमि जिमि तापस कथइ उदासा। तिमि तिम नृपहि उपज विस्वासा॥
en: The more the ascetic spoke of detachment, the more the king's trust grew. When he saw the king under his control in deed, mind and speech, the ascetic, who meditated like a heron waiting for fish, spoke.

first: नाम हमार एकतनु भाई। सुनि नृप बोलेउ पुनि सिर नाई॥
en: 'Brother, my name is Ekatanu.' Hearing this, the king bowed his head and said, 'Explain to me the meaning of your name, knowing me as your own close servant.'

first: दो॰—आदि सृष्टि उपजी जबहि, तब उतपति भइ माेरि।
en: 'I was born when creation first began. I am called Ekatanu, "one body", because I have never taken another body since.'

first: चौ॰—जनि आचरज करहु मन माहीँ। सुत तप तेँ दुर्लभ कछु नाहीँ॥
en: 'Son, do not wonder in your mind; nothing is out of reach through penance. By the power of penance the Creator makes the world, and by the power of penance Vishnu became its protector.'

first: तप बल सम्भु करहिँ सङ्घारा। तप तेँ अगम न कछु संसारा॥
en: 'By the power of penance Shambhu destroys the world. Nothing in the world is beyond reach through penance.' Hearing this, the king grew very fond of him, and he began to tell ancient stories.

first: धरम करम इतिहास अनेका। करइ निरूपन बिरति बिबेका॥
en: He spoke of many stories of dharma and deeds, and explained detachment and wisdom. He told many wonderful tales of the creation, keeping and ending of the world.

first: सुनि महीस तापस बस भयऊ। आपन नाम कहन तब लयऊ॥
en: Hearing them, the king fell under the ascetic's power and was about to tell him his own name. The ascetic said, 'King, I know you. I liked it that you kept it hidden.'

first: सो॰—सुनु महीस असि नीति, जहँ तहँ नाम न कहहिँ नृप।
en: 'Listen, king, it is good policy that kings do not tell their names everywhere. Seeing this cleverness of yours, I have come to love you greatly.'

first: चौ॰—नाम तुम्हार प्रताप-दिनेसा, सत्यकेतु तव पिता नरेसा॥
en: 'Your name is Pratapabhanu, and King Satyaketu is your father. By my guru's grace I know everything, king, but I do not speak of it, knowing it would harm me.'

first: देखि तात तव सहज सुधाई। प्रीति प्रतीति नीति निपुनाई॥
en: 'Son, seeing your natural goodness, your love, trust and skill in right conduct, affection for you has arisen in my mind. So, as you asked, I tell you about myself.'

first: अब प्रसन्न मैं संसय नाहीँ। माँगु जो भूप भाव मन माहीँ॥
en: 'Now I am pleased, without doubt. King, ask for whatever your heart desires.' Hearing these kind words, the king rejoiced, held his feet and begged in many ways.

first: कृपासिन्धु मुनि दरसन तारे। चारि पदारथ करतल माेरे॥
en: 'Merciful sage, by seeing you, the four goals of life are in my hand. Still, seeing my Lord pleased, I will ask for a rare boon and be free of all sorrow.'

first: दो॰—जरा-मरन-दुख रहित तनु, समर जितइ जनि कोउ।
en: 'Let my body be free from old age, death and pain; let no one defeat me in battle; and let me rule the whole earth alone, without an enemy, for a hundred ages of the world.'

first: चौ॰—कह तापस नृप ऐसेइ होऊ। कारन एक कठिन सुनु सोऊ॥
en: The ascetic said, 'King, so be it. But hear of one difficulty. Even Death will bow his head at your feet, except for the race of Brahmins.'

first: तप बल बिप्र सदा बरिआरा। तिन्ह के कोप न कोउ रखवारा॥
en: 'By the power of penance, Brahmins are always strong; no one can save a man from their anger. King, if you win the Brahmins over, then Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva will be in your power.'

first: चल न ब्रह्म-कुल सन बरिआई। सत्य कहउँ दोउ भुजा उठाई॥
en: 'Force does not work against the race of Brahmins; I say this truly, with both arms raised. Listen, king: except by a Brahmin's curse, you will never be destroyed at any time.'

first: हरषेउ राउ बचन सुनि तासू। नाथ न होइ मार अब नासू॥
en: The king rejoiced to hear his words: 'Lord, now I will never be destroyed. By your grace, merciful Lord, all will always be well with me.'

first: दो॰—एवमस्तु कहि कपट-मुनि, बोला कुटिल बहाेरि।
en: Saying 'So be it,' the false sage, full of cunning, spoke again: 'If you tell anyone about meeting me and about losing your way, the fault will not be mine.'

first: चौ॰—ता तेँ मैँ तोहि बरजउँ राजा। कहे कथा तव परम अकाजा॥
en: 'So I warn you, king: telling this story will do you great harm. If this tale reaches a sixth ear, you will be destroyed; my word is true.'

first: यह प्रगटे अथवा द्विज-सापा। नास तोर सुनु भानुप्रतापा॥
en: 'Listen, Bhanupratap: if this becomes known, or by a Brahmin's curse, you will be destroyed. There is no other way you can die, even if Hari and Hara are angry with you.'

first: सत्य नाथ पद-गहि नृप भाखा। द्विज-गुरु-कोप कहहु को राखा॥
en: Holding his feet, the king said, 'True, Lord. Tell me, who can save one from the anger of a Brahmin or a guru? If the Creator is angry, the guru saves; but if one opposes the guru, no one in the world can save him.'

first: जौँ न चलब हम कहे तुम्हारे। होउ नास नहिँ सोच हमारे॥
en: 'If I do not follow your words, let me be destroyed; I do not worry about that. But, Lord, one fear troubles my mind: a Brahmin's curse is very terrible.'

first: दो॰—होहिं बिप्र बस कवनि विधि, कहहु कृपा करि सोउ।
en: 'Kindly tell me how the Brahmins can be won over. Lord kind to the humble, apart from you I see no one who wishes me well.'

first: चौ॰—सुनु नृप बिबिध जतन जग माहीँ। कष्टसाध्य पुनि होहिँ कि नाहीँ॥
en: 'Listen, king, there are many ways in the world, but they are hard to carry out, and even then they may or may not succeed. There is one very easy way, but it has one difficulty.'

first: मम आधीन जुगुति नृप सोई। माेर जाब तव नगर न होई॥
en: 'King, the means is in my hands, but I cannot go to your city. Since I was born, till today, I have never entered anyone's house or village.'

first: जौँ न जाउँ तौ होइ अकाजू। बना आई असमज्जस आजू॥
en: 'If I do not go, your work will fail. So today I am in a fix.' Hearing this, the king spoke gently: 'Lord, the Vedas teach this rule:'

first: बड़े सनेह लघुनह पर करहौँ। गिरि निज सिरन्हि सदा तृन धरहीँ॥
en: 'The great show love to the small. Mountains always carry grass on their heads; the deep ocean bears foam on its crown; the earth always carries dust on its head.'

first: दो॰—अस कहि गहे नरेस पद, स्वामी होहु कृपाल।
en: Saying this, the king held his feet: 'Master, be kind. Lord, you are good and kind to the humble; bear some trouble for my sake.'

first: चौ॰—जानि नृपहि आपन आधीना। बोला तापस कपट-प्रबीना।
en: Knowing the king was in his power, the ascetic, skilled in deceit, said, 'King, I tell you truly: there is nothing in the world I cannot get.'

first: अवसि काज मैँ करिहउँ ताेरा। मन क्रम बचन भगत तैँ मारा।
en: 'I will surely do your work, for you are devoted to me in mind, deed and word. But the power of yoga, penance and mantras bears fruit only when kept secret.'

first: जौँ नरेस मैँ करउँ रसोई। तुम्ह परुसहु मोहि जान न कोई॥
en: 'King, if I cook the food and you serve it, and no one knows about me, then whoever eats that food will do as you command.'

first: पुनि तिन्ह के गृह जेवइँ जोऊ। तव बस होइ भूप सुनु सोऊ॥
en: 'And whoever then eats in their houses will also come under your power, king. Go and carry out this plan, and make a vow to do it for a whole year.'

first: दो॰—नित नूतन द्विज सहस-सत, बरेहु सहित परिवार।
en: 'Each day invite a hundred thousand new Brahmins with their families. For the sake of your vow, I will cook the meal each day.'

first: चौ॰—एहि बिधि भूप कष्ट अति योरे। हाइहहिँ सकल बिप्र बस तोरे॥
en: 'In this way, king, with very little effort, all the Brahmins will come under your power. The Brahmins will perform fire offerings and sacrifices and worship, and through these the gods will easily come under your power too.'

first: अउर एक तोहि कहउँ लखाऊ। मैँ एहि बेष न आउब काऊ।
en: 'I will tell you one more sign: I will never come in this form. King, by my magic I will carry off your family priest.'

first: तप बल तेहि करि आपु समाना। रखिहउँ इहाँ बरप परमाना।
en: 'By the power of penance I will make him like me and keep him here for one year. Listen, king: I will take his form and set all your work right.'

first: गइ निसि बहुत सयन अब कीजे। मोहि तोहि भूप भेँट दिन तोजे।
en: 'Much of the night has passed; now go to sleep. King, you will meet me on the third day. By the power of penance I will take you and your horse home while you sleep.'

first: दो॰—मैँ आउब सोइ वेष धरि, पहिचानेहु तब मोहि।
en: 'I will come in that form; know me then, when I call you aside and tell you this whole story.'

first: चौ॰—सयन कीन्ह नृप आयसु मानी। आसन जाइ बैठ छल-ज्ञानी॥
en: Obeying his word, the king lay down, and the master of tricks went and sat on his seat. The tired king fell fast asleep, but how could the other sleep, with his worries growing?

first: कालकेतु निसिचर तहँ आवा। जेहि सूकर होइ नृपहि भुलावा॥
en: Then the demon Kalaketu came there, who had become the boar and led the king astray. He was a close friend of the ascetic king and was a master of many tricks.

first: तेहि के सत सुत अरु दस भाई। खल अति अजय देव-दुख-दाई॥
en: He had a hundred sons and ten brothers, very wicked and hard to defeat, who troubled the gods. Seeing Brahmins, saints and gods suffering, the king had earlier killed them all in battle.

first: तेहि खल पाछिल बयर सँभारा। तापस नृप मिलि मन्त्र बिचारा॥
en: That wicked one remembered the old hatred. He met the ascetic king and they made a plan, and they set up a scheme to destroy their enemy. Ruled by fate, the king knew nothing of it.

first: दो॰—रिपु तेजसी अकेल अपि, लघु करि गनिय न ताहु।
en: A powerful enemy, even if alone, should not be thought of as small. Even now Rahu, who is only a head, troubles the sun and the moon.

first: चौ॰—तापस नूप निज सखहि निहारी। हरपि मिलेउ उठि भयउ सुखारी॥
en: Seeing his friend, the ascetic king rose gladly to meet him and was happy. He told his friend the whole story, and the demon was pleased and said,

first: अब साधेउँ रिपु सुनहु नरेसा। जौँ तुम्ह कीन्ह मोर उपदेसा॥
en: 'Listen, king, now I have got our enemy in hand, since you have done as I advised. Give up your worry and sleep now; the Creator has cured the disease without medicine.'

first: कुल समेत रिपु-मूल बहाई। चौथे दिवस मिलब मैँ आई॥
en: 'I will wipe out the enemy, root and all, with his family, and come to meet you on the fourth day.' After comforting the ascetic king well, the great cheat set off, full of rage.

first: भानुप्रतापहि बाजि समेता। पहुँचायेसि छत माँझ निकेता॥
en: In a moment he took Pratapabhanu and his horse home. He laid the king to sleep beside the queen and tied the horse properly in the stable.

first: दो॰—राजा के उपरोहितहि, हरि लेइ गयउ बहोरि।
en: Then he carried off the king's family priest. Clouding his mind with magic, he took him and kept him in a mountain cave.

first: चो॰—आपु बिरचि उपरोहित रूपा। परेउ जाइ तेहि सेज अनूपा॥
en: He himself took the form of the priest and went and lay on his fine bed. The king woke before dawn and was greatly surprised to find himself at home.

first: मुनि महिमा मन महँ अनुमानी। उठेउ गँवहिँ जेहि जान न रानी॥
en: Thinking in his mind of the sage's power, he rose quietly so that the queen would not know. He mounted the same horse and went to the forest, and none of the men or women of the city knew.

first: गये जाम जुग भूपति आवा। घर घर उत्सव बाज बघावा॥
en: After half a day had passed the king returned, and in every house there was celebration and music. When the king saw the priest, he looked at him in wonder, remembering the plan.

first: जुग सम नृपहि गयउ दिन तीनी। कपटी मुनि-पद रहि मति लीनी।
en: The three days passed like ages for the king, his mind fixed on the false sage's feet. Knowing the time had come, the priest came and told the king everything in private.

first: दो॰—नृप हरषेउ पहिचानि गुरु, भ्रम-बल रहा न चेत।
en: Recognising his guru, the king rejoiced; under delusion he had no sense left. At once he invited a hundred thousand fine Brahmins with their families.

first: चौ॰—उपरोहित जेवनार बनाई। छरस चारि बिधि जसि स्त्रुति गाई॥
en: The priest prepared a feast of the six tastes and four kinds, as the scriptures describe. He made the food by magic, with so many dishes that no one could count them.

first: बिबिध मृगन्ह कर आमिष राँधा। तेहि महँ बिप्र मास खल साँधा॥
en: He cooked the meat of many kinds of animals, and into it the wicked one mixed the flesh of Brahmins. The king called all the Brahmins to the meal, washed their feet and seated them.

first: परुसन जबहिँ लाग महिपाला। भइ अकास-वानी तेहि काला॥
en: Just as the king began to serve, a voice came from the sky: 'Brahmins, rise and go home. Do not eat this food; it will do great harm.'

first: भयउ रसाेई भूसुर मासू। सब द्विज उठे मानि बिस्वासू॥
en: 'The food has been made with Brahmin flesh!' Believing the voice, all the Brahmins rose. The king was stunned, his mind lost in confusion; ruled by fate, he could not say a word.

first: दो॰—बोले बिप्र सकोप तब, नहिँ कछु कीन्ह बिचार।
en: Then the Brahmins, in anger and without stopping to think, said, 'Foolish king, go and be born a demon, with all your family!'

first: चौ॰—छत्रबन्धु तैँ बिप्र बोलाई। घालइ लिये सहित समुदाई॥
en: 'Low warrior, you called Brahmins here to ruin them along with their families. God has saved our dharma; you will be destroyed with all your family.'

first: सम्बत मध्य नास तव होऊ। जलदाता न रहिहि कुल कोऊ॥
en: 'Within a year you will be destroyed, and no one will be left in your family to offer you water.' Hearing the curse, the king was very upset and afraid. Then again a fine voice came from the sky:

first: बिप्रहु साप बिचारि न दीन्हा। नहिँ अपराध भूप कछु कीन्हा॥
en: 'Brahmins, you gave the curse without thinking; the king has done no wrong.' Hearing the voice from the sky, all the Brahmins were amazed, and the king went to the kitchen.

first: तहँ न असन नहिँ बिप्र सुआरा। फिरेउ राउ मन सोच अपारा॥
en: There was neither food nor the Brahmin cook. The king came back with endless worry in his mind. He told the Brahmins the whole story and fell to the ground, frightened and distressed.

first: दो॰—भूपति भावी मिटइ नहिँ, जदपि न दूषन तोर।
en: 'King, though you are not at fault, fate cannot be wiped out. A Brahmin's curse is very terrible; nothing can make it otherwise.'

first: चौ॰—अस कहि सब महिदेव सिधाये। समाचार पुरबासिन्ह पाये॥
en: Saying this, all the Brahmins left, and the people of the city heard the news. They grieved and blamed the Creator, who had set out to make a swan and made a crow instead.

first: उपरोहितहि भवन पहुँचाई। असुर असुर तापसहि खबरि जनाई॥
en: The demon took the priest back home and sent word to the ascetic. That wicked one sent letters everywhere, and all the kings came with their armies ready.

first: घेरेन्हि नगर निसान बजाई। बिबिध भाँति नित होइ लराई॥
en: They beat their drums and surrounded the city, and fighting of many kinds went on every day. All the brave warriors fought and fell after doing great deeds, and the king fell to the ground with his brother.

first: सत्यकेतु-कुल कोउ नहिँ बाचा। बिप्र-साप किमि होइ असाँचा॥
en: No one of Satyaketu's family was left; how could a Brahmin's curse prove false? Having defeated their enemy, the kings resettled the city and went home with the glory of victory.

first: दो॰—भरद्वाज सुनु जाहि जत्ब, हाेइ बिधाता बाम।
en: Yajnavalkya said: 'Bharadvaja, listen: when the Creator turns against someone, dust becomes like Mount Meru to him, a father like Death, and a rope like a snake.'

first: चौ॰—काल पाइ मुनि सुनु सोइ राजा। भयउ निसाचर सहित समाजा।
en: 'Listen, sage: in time that king was born a demon with all his people. He had ten heads and twenty arms, and was the mighty warrior named Ravana.'

first: भूप अनुज अरिमर्दन नामा। भयउ सो कुम्भकरन बल धामा
en: 'The king's younger brother, named Arimardana, became Kumbhakarna, a store of strength. His minister, who was named Dharmaruchi, became his younger half-brother,'

first: नाम विभीषन जेहि जग जाना। बिष्नु-भगत विज्ञान-निधाना॥
en: 'named Vibhishana, known to the world as a devotee of Vishnu and a treasure of wisdom. The king's sons and servants became many fierce demons.'

first: काम-रूप खल जिनिस अनेका। कुटिल भयङ्कर बिगत-विधेका॥
en: 'Wicked ones of many kinds who could take any form at will; crooked, fearful and without sense, merciless, violent and sinful; they troubled the whole world beyond description.'

first: दो॰—उपजे जदपि पुलस्त्य-कुल; पावन अमल अनूप।
en: 'Though they were born in the family of Pulastya, pure, spotless and matchless, still, by the Brahmins' curse, they all became sin in bodily form.'

first: चौ॰—कीन्ह बिबिध तप तीनिउँ भाई। परम उन नहिं बरनि सो जाई।
en: 'The three brothers did penance of many kinds, so severe it cannot be described. Seeing their penance, Brahma went near and said, "Son, I am pleased; ask for a boon."'

first: करि बिनती पद गहि दससीसा। बोलेउ बचन सुनहु जगदीसा॥
en: 'The ten-headed one held his feet, begged and said, "Lord of the world, listen: let us not die at anyone's hands except the two races of monkeys and men."'

first: एवमस्तु तुम्ह बड़ तप कीन्हा। मैँ ब्रह्मा मिलि तेहि बर दीन्हा॥
en: 'Brahma and I granted him the boon: "So be it; you have done great penance." Then Brahma went to Kumbhakarna, and seeing him he was amazed in his mind.'

first: जौँ एहि खल नित करब अहारू। होइहि सत्र उजार संसारू॥
en: '"If this wicked one eats every day, the whole world will be laid waste." So Brahma sent Sarasvati to turn his mind, and he asked for sleep for six months at a time.'

first: दो॰—गये बिभीषन पास पुनि, कहेउ पुत्र घर माँगु।
en: 'Then Brahma went to Vibhishana and said, "Son, ask for a boon." He asked for pure love for the Lord's lotus feet.'

first: चौ॰—तिन्हहिं देइ बर ब्रह्म सिधाये। हरषित ते अपने गृह आये॥
en: 'Brahma gave them their boons and went away, and they came home glad. Maya's daughter, named Mandodari, was very beautiful, a jewel among women.'

first: सोइ मय दीन्हि रावनहि आनी। होइहि जातुधान-पति जानी॥
en: 'Maya brought her and gave her to Ravana, knowing he would become king of the demons. Ravana was glad to get a fine wife, and then he went and arranged marriages for his two brothers.'

first: गिरि-त्रिकूट एक सिन्धु मँझारी। बिधि-निर्मित दुर्गम अति मारी॥
en: 'In the middle of the sea was a mountain called Trikuta, made by Brahma, very large and hard to reach. The demon Maya rebuilt it with countless palaces of gold set with jewels.'

first: भोगावति जसि अहि-कुल बासा। अमरावति जसि सक्र-निवासा॥
en: 'Like Bhogavati, home of the serpent race, and Amaravati, home of Indra, but even more lovely and splendid, was that city known to the world as Lanka.'

first: दो॰—खाँई सिन्धु गंभीर अति, चारिहु दिसि फिरि आव।
en: 'The very deep sea ran all around it like a moat. Its strong golden walls were set with jewels; their making cannot be described.'

first: हरि प्रेरित जेहि कलप जोइ, जातुधान-पति होइ।
en: 'In whatever age, by Hari's will, someone becomes king of the demons, that brave, glorious one of matchless strength lives there with his army.'

first: चौ॰—रहे तहाँ निसिचर भट भारे। ते सब सुरम्ह समर सङ्घारे।
en: 'Great demon warriors had lived there before, but the gods killed them all in battle. Now, by Indra's order, millions of guards of Kubera, lord of the yakshas, lived there.'

first: दसमुख कतहुँ खबरि असि पाई। सेन साजि गढ़ घेरेसि जाई॥
en: 'Somewhere Ravana heard this news. He gathered his army and went and surrounded the fort. Seeing the huge army of fierce warriors, the yakshas fled for their lives.'

first: फिरि सब नगर दसानन देखा। गयउ सोच सुख भयउ बिसेखा॥
en: 'Ravana went round and saw the whole city. His worries left him and he was very happy. Thinking it lovely by nature and hard to reach, he made it his capital.'

first: जेहि जस जोग बाँटि गृह दीन्हे। सुखो सकल रजनीचर कीन्हे॥
en: 'He gave out houses to each as was fitting and made all the demons happy. Once he attacked Kubera and brought back the Pushpaka chariot as his prize.'

first: दो॰—कौतुकहो कैलास पुनि, लीन्हेसि जाइ उठाइ।
en: 'Then, as if in sport, he went and lifted up Kailasa, as if testing the strength of his arms, and went away very pleased.'

first: चौ॰—सुख सम्पति सुत सेन सहाई। जय प्रताप बल बुद्धि बड़ाई॥
en: 'His joy, wealth, sons, army, helpers, victories, glory, strength, wisdom and fame kept growing every day, just as greed grows with every gain.'

first: अति बल कुम्भकरन असभ्राता। जेहि कहँ नहिँ प्रतिभट जग जाता॥
en: 'He had such a brother as the very mighty Kumbhakarna, whose equal in battle was never born in the world. He drank and slept for six months, and when he woke the three worlds trembled.'

first: जौँ दिन-प्रति अहार कर साेई। बिस्व बेगि सब चौपट हाई॥
en: 'If he ate every day, the whole world would soon be ruined. He was steady in battle beyond description, and there were countless other strong warriors like him.'

first: बारिदनाद जेठ सुत तासू। भठ महँ प्रथम लोक जग जासू॥
en: 'Ravana's eldest son was Meghanada, who was counted first among the world's warriors. No one could face him in battle, and in the city of the gods there was always a rush to flee.'

first: दो॰—कुमुख अकम्पन कुलिसरद, धूमकेतु अतिकाय।
en: 'Durmukha, Akampana, Vajradanta, Dhumaketu, Atikaya and many such warriors were there, each of whom could conquer the world alone.'

first: चौ॰—काम-रूप जानहिँ सब माया। सपनेहुँ जिन्ह के धरम न दाया॥
en: 'They could take any form at will and knew every trick; they had no dharma or mercy, not even in dreams. Once the ten-headed one sat in his court and looked at his countless family.'

first: सुत-समूह जन परिजन नाती। गनइ को पार निसाचर जाती॥
en: 'Crowds of sons, kinsmen, servants and grandsons: who can count the race of demons? Seeing his army, Ravana, proud by nature, spoke words full of anger and arrogance.'

first: सुनहु सकल रजनीचर जूया। हमरे बैरी बिबुध-बरूया॥
en: '"Listen, all you demon bands: the host of gods is our enemy. They do not fight face to face; seeing a strong enemy, they run away."'

first: तिन्ह कर मरन एक बिधि हाेई। कहउँ बुझाइ सुनहु अब साेई॥
en: '"There is one way to kill them; now listen, and I will explain it. Go and stop everything: feeding Brahmins, sacrifices, fire offerings and rites for the dead."'

first: दो॰—छुधा-छीन बल-हीन सुर, सहजहि मिलिहहिँ आइ।
en: '"Weak from hunger and without strength, the gods will come and give in easily. Then, once they are fully in my power, I will either kill them or let them go."'

first: चौ॰—मेघनाद कहँ पुनि हँकरावा। दीन्ही सिख बल बयर बढ़ावा॥
en: 'Then he called Meghanada and taught him, stirring up his strength and hatred: "The gods who are steady and strong in battle and proud of their fighting,'

first: तिन्हहिँ जीति रन आनेसु बाँधी। उठि सुन पितु-अनुसासन काँधी॥
en: '"conquer them in battle and bring them here in chains." The son rose and accepted his father's command. In this way Ravana gave orders to all, and he himself set out with a mace in his hand.'

first: चलत दसानन डोलसि अवनी। गर्जत गर्भ-स्त्रवत सुर-रवनो॥
en: 'As the ten-headed one marched, the earth shook, and at his roar the wives of the gods lost their unborn children. Hearing that Ravana was coming in anger, the gods hid in the caves of Mount Meru.'

first: दिगपालन्ह के लोक सुहाये। सूने सकल दसानन पाये॥
en: 'Ravana found all the lovely worlds of the guardians of the directions empty. Again and again he roared loudly like a lion and shouted insults to challenge the gods.'

first: रन-मद मत्त फिरइ जग धावा। प्रतिभट खोजत कतहुँ न पावा॥
en: 'Drunk with the passion for battle, he rushed all over the world looking for an equal fighter, but found none anywhere. The sun, moon, wind, Varuna, Kubera, Fire, Time and Yama, all who held power,'

first: किन्नर सिद्ध मनुज सुर नागा। हठि सबहो के पन्धहि लागा॥
en: 'kinnaras, siddhas, men, gods and serpents, he forcibly went after them all. As far as Brahma's creation reaches, all embodied men and women came under the ten-headed one's rule.'

first: आयसु कहिँ सकल भयभीता। नवहिँ आइ नित चरन बिनीता ॥७॥
en: 'All of them, in fear, did as he ordered, and came humbly every day to bow at his feet.'

first: दो॰—भुज-बल बिस्व बस्य करि, राखेसि कोउ न स्वतन्त्र।
en: 'Having brought the world under his rule by the strength of his arms, he left no one free. Ravana, jewel among kings, ruled by his own will.'

first: देव जच्छ गन्धर्व नर, किन्नर नाग कुमारि।
en: 'The daughters of gods, yakshas, gandharvas, men, kinnaras and serpents, many lovely and fine women, he won by the strength of his arms and married.'

first: चौ॰—इन्द्रजीत सन जो कछु कहेऊ। सो सब जनु पहिलेहि करि रहेऊ॥
en: 'Whatever he told Indrajit to do, it was as if that son had done it already. Now hear what was done by those to whom he had first given orders.'

first: देखत भीम-रूप सब पापी। निसिचर-निकर देव-परितापी॥
en: 'All the bands of demons, fearful to look at, sinful and tormenting the gods, made trouble everywhere, taking many forms by magic.'

first: जेहि बिधि होइ धरम-निर्मूला। सो सब करहिँ बेद-प्रतिकूला॥
en: 'They did everything against the Vedas that would tear dharma out by the roots. In whatever land they found cows and Brahmins, they set fire to the towns, villages and cities.'

first: सुभ-आचरन कतहुँ नहिँ होई। देव बिप्र गुरु मान न कोई॥
en: 'Good conduct was found nowhere; no one honoured gods, Brahmins or gurus. There was no devotion to Hari, no sacrifice, prayer or giving; the Vedas and Puranas were not heard even in dreams.'

first: जप जोग बिरागा, तप मख-भागा, स्त्रवन सुनइ दससीसा।
en: 'If the ten-headed one heard of prayer, yoga, detachment, penance or sacrifice, he rushed there himself; nothing was allowed to remain, and he seized and destroyed it all. The world became so corrupt that dharma was not heard of. Anyone who spoke the Vedas and Puranas he terrified in many ways and drove out of the land.'

first: सो॰—बरनि न जाइ अनीति, घोर निसाचर जो करहिँ।
en: 'The cruel wrongs that the terrible demons did cannot be described. What limit can there be to the sins of those who so love violence?'

first: चौ॰—बाढ़े खल बहु चार जुआरा। जे लम्पट पर-धन पर-दारा॥
en: 'Wicked men, thieves and gamblers grew in number, men who lusted after others' wealth and others' wives. They did not honour mother, father or the gods, and made holy men serve them.'

first: जिन्ह के यह आचरन भवानी। ते जानहु निसिचर सम प्रानी॥
en: 'Bhavani, know that creatures who behave like this are like demons. Seeing such great harm to dharma, the earth grew very frightened and distressed.'

first: गिरि सरि सिन्धु भार नहिँ मोही। जस मोहि गरुअ एक पर-द्रोही।
en: '"Mountains, rivers and seas are no burden to me, as heavy as one who harms others." She saw all dharma turned upside down, but out of fear of Ravana she could say nothing.'

first: धेनु-रूप धरि हृदय बिचारी। गई तहाँ जहँ सुर-मुनि-झारी॥
en: 'After thinking it over, she took the form of a cow and went to where the gods and sages were gathered. Weeping, she told them her sorrow, but none of them could do anything.'

first: सुर मुनि गन्धर्बा, मिलि करि सर्बा, गे बिरज्चि के लोका।
en: 'The gods, sages and gandharvas all went together to Brahma's world. With them went the poor Earth in the form of a cow, very distressed with fear and grief. Brahma understood everything and thought, "I too can do nothing. He whose servant you are, the undying one, will help both you and us."'

first: सो॰—धरनि घरहि मन धीर, कह बिरज्चि हरि-पद सुमिरु।
en: '"Earth, keep courage in your mind," said Brahma, "and remember Hari's feet. The Lord knows the pain of his people; he will crush this terrible trouble."'

first: चौ॰—ब्रैठे सुर सब करहिँ बिचारा। कहँ पाइय प्रभु करिय पुकारा।
en: 'All the gods sat and talked it over: where could they find the Lord to call on him? Some said they should go to Vaikuntha; some said the Lord lives in the ocean of milk.'

first: जाके हृदय भगति जसि प्रीती। प्रभु तहँ प्रगट सदा तेहि रीती॥
en: 'The Lord always appears to each person according to the devotion and love in his heart. Girija, I was in that gathering, and when the moment came I said one thing.'

first: हरि ब्यापक सर्वत्र समाना। प्रेम तेँ प्रगट हाेहिँ मैँ जाना॥
en: '"Hari is present everywhere alike; I know that he appears through love. In what place, time, direction or corner is the Lord not present?"'

first: अग-जग-मय सब रहित बिरागी। प्रेम तेँ प्रभु प्रगटइ जिमि आगी॥
en: '"He is in all moving and unmoving things, yet apart from all and free of attachment. Through love the Lord appears, like fire." My words pleased everyone, and Brahma praised them, saying, "Well said, well said."'

first: दो॰—सुनि बिरज्चि मन हरषि तन,-पुलकि नयन बह नीर।
en: 'Hearing this, Brahma was glad at heart; his body thrilled and tears flowed from his eyes. The steady-minded one joined his hands and, with full attention, began to praise the Lord.'

first: जय जय सुर-नायक, जन सुख-दायक, प्रनतपाल भगवन्ता।
en: 'Victory, victory to the lord of the gods, giver of joy to his people, protector of those who bow to him! Friend of cows and Brahmins, enemy of demons, dear husband of the ocean's daughter, victory to you! Protector of the gods and the earth, whose deeds are wonderful and whose secret no one knows, you who are kind by nature and merciful to the humble, show us your grace.'

first: जय जय अबिनासी, सन घट बासी, व्यापक परमानन्दा।
en: 'Victory, victory to the undying one, who lives in every heart, present everywhere, supreme bliss; beyond knowing and beyond the senses, of holy deeds, free of maya, giver of freedom. Victory to him who is being, awareness and bliss, on whom crowds of sages, free of delusion, detached and full of love, meditate night and day and whose virtues they sing.'

first: जेहि सृष्टि उपाई, त्रिबिधि बनाई, सङ्ग सहाय न दूजा।
en: 'He who made creation in three ways, with no other companion or helper, may that destroyer of sin think of us; we know neither devotion nor worship. He destroys the fear of worldly life, delights the minds of sages and crushes hosts of troubles. In mind, word and deed, giving up our cleverness, all the gods come to him for shelter.'

first: सारद स्त्रुति सेषा, रिषय असेषा, जा कहँ कोउ नहिँ जाना।
en: 'Whom Sarasvati, the Vedas, Shesha and all the sages cannot know, to whom, as the Vedas proclaim, the humble are dear, may that blessed Lord be moved to pity. He is the Mandara mountain to churn the ocean of worldly life, lovely in every way, a temple of virtues and a mass of joy. All sages, siddhas and gods, deeply afraid, bow at the Lord's lotus feet.'

first: दो॰—जानि सभय सुर-भूमि सुनि, बचन समेत सनेह।
en: Knowing the gods and the Earth were afraid, and hearing their loving words, a deep voice came from the sky that removed their grief and doubt.
